issues.message: stone_bricks is 58 % of the build: break it up with a second material.

visual.summary: Keep level 1: a big four-towered stone keep with a gate, windows and a throne hall; grand, though the tower tops look like open boxes.
problems: Level 3 only adds vines over level 2: give it its own feature, such as timber hoardings (wooden galleries) on the towers or steep dark conical roofs on two of them.
It is grey stone brick almost everywhere (56 to 58 %): a dark oak timber element (hoarding, gate canopy, roof) would tie it to the rest of the kingdom's look.
On level 1 the tower tops are open boxes; even a simple slab cap or a stair parapet would make them look finished.

issues.message: stone_bricks is 58 % of the build: break it up with a second material.

notes.artefacts: Carlton's newest note (bigger, a grand hall and a throne for the king, levels more different) is not addressed yet

visual.summary: A solid square stone brick keep with four corner towers, a plinth and a dark oak door frame. The new tower caps read as flat wooden lids with a stick in the middle, and it does not yet have the grand hall and throne Carlton asked for.
problems: Carlton's newest note: make it bigger, with a grand hall and a throne for the king (a raised dais with a stair throne, red carpet runner, banners and chandeliers), and make each level add a clear function, not just decoration
The tower caps look like flat brown lids with a single fence post: use steep dark oak or spruce stair cones (at least 3 steps high) or keep the battlements open with a flagpole and banner
Still almost all grey stone brick and no life: a few vines, a banner over the door, lanterns by the entrance

visual.summary: A compact, symmetric stone keep with four corner turrets under dark caps, battlements and a central door. Tidy and coherent, clearly the seed the bigger levels grow from.
problems: The turret caps are stepped tiers with a wide flared skirt, which reads more like a pagoda than a medieval tower: make them steep cones (a stair ring with one block of overhang, then 3 or 4 rings narrowing by one each step, finished with a slab and the flagpole), so they are taller than they are wide
Nothing alive yet: a banner over the door or two lanterns either side would help L1
Our QC renders of a structure this big are washed out by fog (renderer, not the build); judged from the near parts

visual.summary: The compact symmetric keep with four turrets, now under steep dark cones with flagpoles that read as medieval spires. Every room can be walked to.
problems: Still nothing alive at L1: a banner over the door or two lanterns either side

Reachability (flood fill from the ground outside, soldiers half a block tall, jump 1, drop 3, ladders climb): every floor, room, wall walk and tower top is reached; only the roof cones, the tie beams under the hall roof and the tops of log piles and the low forecourt wall are not, which is right
